message.content:
Yes – you can file a noise‑complaint with the City of Atlanta.  
In Atlanta, noise complaints are handled by the **City Police Department** (or the City’s Code Enforcement office) and the city’s **311** system. The city council can’t take the complaint directly, but they can forward it to the appropriate department.

### How to file a noise complaint in Atlanta

| Method | What to do | Contact |
|--------|------------|---------|
| **Phone** | Call the 311 service (free from any phone). | 404‑656‑3111 |
| **Online** | Use the City of Atlanta’s online portal to submit a noise complaint. | https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 |
| **In‑person** | Visit the City Police Department or the City Code Enforcement office. | 404‑656‑3111 (for police) |
| **Mail** | Send a written complaint to the City Police Department. | 404‑656‑3111 |

### What information to provide

- Your name and contact details (optional, but helpful)
- Date, time, and location of the noise
- Description of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs)
- Any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings)

### Legal background

Atlanta’s noise ordinance is part of the **City Code** under the **Public Safety** category. The ordinance sets limits on decibel levels and specifies quiet hours (typically 10 p.m.–7 a.m. on weekdays and 11 p.m.–7 a.m. on weekends). Violations can result in fines or other enforcement actions.

If you’re unsure whether your situation falls under the ordinance, you can ask the 311 operator or the police officer handling the complaint for clarification.

---

**Quick tip:** If you’re dealing with a recurring issue, keep a log of dates, times, and any responses you receive. This can help the city track patterns and enforce the ordinance more effectively.
